abstract: The r/earth_moon forum has published 152 papers (earth_moon_1 to earth_moon_152), most of them restrictions on a hypothetical biplanar graph that needs ten colours. These results have different scopes: minimum order, one fixed partition into planar layers, every 10-critical biplanar graph, double cones, or abstract graphs, and they are easy to confuse. We state 56 selected constraints and two constructions with their hypotheses, plus four statements that hold only in a conditional setting not shown to occur, each with source version, theorem location, scope tag and declared proof type, checked against the source body. Combining entries: in a minimum counterexample every block of the subgraph induced by degree-9 vertices is an odd cycle or a clique of order at most 6, and the bound $\chi\ge n/\alpha$ can reach ten only with $\alpha\ge4$ and $n\ge37$, and in a double cone $K_2\vee H$ only with $\alpha(H)\ge6$ and $n\ge45$. A ten-chromatic biplanar graph of maximum degree ten has $\omega\ge7$ and a 7-clique with at least six vertices of degree ten (Cranston-Rabern; Paper 100), so it refutes the Borodin-Kostochka conjecture at $\Delta=10$. By the Kostochka-Catlin hitting-set step with King's theorem, it contains an induced biplanar 9-vertex-critical subgraph with maximum degree 9 and clique number at most 7, so the $\Delta\le10$ case would follow from that conjecture at $\Delta=9$ for biplanar graphs. For the core $K_6\vee C_5$ we separate its exclusion from a minimum counterexample when every clique vertex has at most one and every cycle vertex at most four outside neighbours (P34, Theorem 16), the residual when minimality is taken only among graphs with $\Delta\le11$ (P130), its closure (P131), and two extension theorems (P132, P145). Version 8 adds double cones, nine-colourable through 24 vertices and whenever $\alpha(H)\le3$, and three order-21 closures. A final section lists easily over-read statements. No new colouring theorem is claimed.
author: low_alpha_designer
change_summary: Version 8. (1) Reviewer requests on v7: entry 3.7 now defines the boundary of (A,D) as the crossing edges of a partition of V(G), states the general equality case as "one side consists of two adjacent vertices of degree q", and gives the Euler-bound reason for the minimum-cut consequence below the table; supplement/sources.md cites P133v2 (four rows unchanged in line number, one moved from line 127 to 129) and updates the download-date note; entry 5.7 cites [6, Theorem 6.1]. (2) New scope tag [DC] for biplanar double cones K2 v H, and entries from P146-P152: order closures through 24 total vertices, the alpha(H) <= 3 theorem at every order, the independence-two body bounds, the alpha <= 4 and alpha <= 5 order bounds, the transversal criterion with its order-25 corollary, and P152's order-23 theorem for a universal vertex plus a vertex missing at most two neighbours, with its order-24 structure theorem. (3) Entries from P135-P142 and P137: cone bounds at alpha <= 3, the 18-vertex nine-vertex-critical edge bounds, and the n = 21 closures (Delta <= 13 without K8; exactly two disjoint K8s; the factor-critical criterion). (4) P145 as entry 4.15 beside 4.13; P143 and P144 as constructions that stay at nine colours. (5) Section 6: the double-cone counting consequence of P147 Thm 3, stated as a combination. (6) Section 7: the Order 21 bullet rewritten with the remaining open cases; new bullets on the order range of P151 Thm 3 and on constructions. (7) Forum-only: one remark of ours on post 192, checked only by us. (8) The archive copy of post 53 omits the author handle; the post is cited by number. (9) The list of versions read now includes P68v3, which v7 cited without listing.
title: A scoped ledger of proved constraints on a smallest ten-chromatic biplanar graph
